supersedes.why: The decision owner found it legally overbroad: it was labelled for arrests or charges without conviction under (1)(c) and delivered the acquittal packet, so a participant who was never charged and one who was acquitted resolved to the same configuration under the wrong subsection for one of them.

sharedBaseAsset.statement: The same statewide OJD form serves all three. What distinguishes them is the option selected on it, and the decision permits the shared base asset expressly while forbidding the three from resolving to one generic or null configuration.

architecture.shape: one packet family, three governed configurations
architecture.permittedBecause: The decision permits one family with multiple configurations only where each configuration has a distinct stable identity and cannot be selected by the wrong disposition. Each has its own configuration id, route id, packet set, required facts, disposition predicate and specification hash, and each predicate names what it refuses.

configurations.label: NEVER CHARGED
configurations.formOptionText: I was cited or arrested and there was no court case. I am moving to set aside the citation or arrest records.

refuses: any disposition that followed a filed charge
dispositionPredicate.whyItRefuses: The decision owner recorded that paragraph (1)(c) applies ONLY when no accusatory instrument was filed, and that this configuration may not accept an acquittal or an ordinary dismissal as an equivalent disposition.

requiredFacts.proves: the prosecuting attorney elected not to proceed
exact arrest, citation, or charge identity

configurations.sixtyDayRule: The form's own instruction: file 60 days after the prosecutor says they will not file charges. The alternative it offers -- file any time after dismissal or acquittal -- belongs to the (1)(d) configurations and is deliberately not available here.

sourceIdentities.officialTitle: Oregon State Police Set-Aside Criminal History Request and Instructions

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Oregon State Police LEDS criminal history. Use the Oregon State Police set-aside criminal history request and instructions, retained in Edition 1.2, or the Oregon Judicial Department request for a set-aside criminal record check. The LEDS history fixes the offence class, the disposition and the sentence-completion dates, and it is obtained before anything is drafted.

Check your answer to "What was the offence called, which ORS section was cited, and on what date did it happen?" against Oregon State Police LEDS criminal history, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Evidence of the prosecutor's declination and its date. Ask the prosecuting attorney's office, or check the circuit court file, for the document or docket entry showing the state elected not to proceed and when. This is the gate for the whole track, because the 60 days runs from it.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The prosecuting attorney's office, or the circuit court file

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "On what date did the prosecutor say the state would not go forward with the case?" against Evidence of the prosecutor's declination and its date, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain A full set of fingerprints. Have a full set of fingerprints taken on a fingerprint card, or in any other manner the Department of State Police specifies, and forward them to the department with its fee. ORS 137.225(2)(c) and (2)(d).
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: A law enforcement agency or an authorised fingerprinting service

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "What is your full legal name, and have you used any other names?" against A full set of fingerprints, and correct the packet if they disagree.
Signature on the declaration under penalty of perjury — Motion and declaration.
Fingerprinting and forwarding the card to the Department of State Police with the fee — Outside the court packet, sent to OSP.
The judge's signature and findings on the proposed order — Proposed order.
Filing the motion and serving the prosecuting attorney — The circuit court and the prosecutor's office.
The participant signs the motion and declaration under penalty of perjury.
None required. ORS 137.225(13)(a) allows a declaration under penalty of perjury in place of an affidavit.

No court filing fee: ORS 137.225(1)(g) provides that a person filing a motion under the section is not required to pay the filing fee established under ORS 21.135. The Department of State Police charges a record-check fee not exceeding the actual cost, and where only one record check is performed it may charge only one fee regardless of the number of counties filed in. The prosecuting attorney may not charge a fee.
not applicable to the court filing. There is no filing fee to waive.
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only when the participant cannot pay the filing fee.

participantActionRequired.description: A copy of the motion is served on the office of the prosecuting attorney who had authority to prosecute the charge.
File the motion and proposed order in the circuit court of the county in which the person was arrested, cited or charged, at any time after 60 days from the prosecutor's declination.

configurations.label: ACQUITTAL
configurations.formOptionText: There was a court case, and I am not moving to set aside any convictions. I am moving to set aside all eligible dismissed or acquitted charges only.

refuses: a citation or arrest with no court case
any conviction being set aside on this configuration
dispositionPredicate.whyItRefuses: Option 2 is available only where there was a court case. A participant who was never charged has no case to name on it.

requiredFacts.proves: no conviction is being set aside on this configuration

configurations.label: ORDINARY DISMISSAL
configurations.formOptionText: There was a court case, and I am not moving to set aside any convictions. I am moving to set aside all eligible dismissed or acquitted charges only.

refuses: a citation or arrest with no court case
an acquittal, which is its own configuration
dispositionPredicate.whyItRefuses: Acquittal and dismissal share Option 2 on the form and share a subsection, and they are still two dispositions. Giving them one configuration is what produced the overbroad route this replaces.
